sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

Case N32: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 181x181x137 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case N32 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(181, 181, 137) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: peripheral nerve sheath tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 68/137 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking:
I'm trying to work out the scale of the coronal view against the full slice count, estimating the mass's height at roughly 65mm and checking how that maps to the axial slice range, noting there seems to be a thin tail portion near the bottom.

Mapping coronal y-coordinates to axial slice indices, I'm figuring the mass spans roughly k=22-87 with thinner tails extending from 3-102, likely corresponding to nerve tissue continuing beyond the main tumor body. I want to verify this by checking sagittal and axial views with the outline overlay at specific slices like 10 and 95.

content.text: sheet axial 3–102/137 (12 slices) | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking lower, around slices 12-25, there's a bright round structure near the tumor edge that could be a vessel — likely a popliteal vein given its position and the green outline enclosing it around slice 21. The tumor itself seems to extend roughly from slice 22 to 28, with this vascular structure trailing below it.

I should zoom into slices 21-27 and also check the upper range around 84-93 to clarify what's happening at both ends. Let me start by examining axial slices 25 and 21 more closely.

axial 84/137 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At axial slice 24, that bright round structure near the tumor is likely a vein similar to ones seen in slices 0 and 12, sitting adjacent to where the tumor tapers and the nerve emerges. I should check the sagittal and coronal views of the mask to see how the tumor's tail extends.

I'm thinking slices 3-20 are too thin and should probably be trimmed, so my strategy is to cut the mask below slice 22 and above slice 90 using erase tools, but first I want to view the sagittal through the mask to pin down the actual limits.

content.text: sagittal 113/181 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Using the pixel-to-mm scale from the sagittal image, I calculate the mass spans roughly 67mm vertically. I'm also checking whether the dim region at the top right of the sagittal slice represents extension of the mass into the posterior-superior tissue.

I need to figure out where the tumor tails off inferiorly — there are bright round structures across several axial slices (12, 18, 21, 24) that look like vessels rather than tumor, and I'm trying to distinguish those from the actual lesion boundary. It seems the mass tapers down near the tibial nerve around slice 10-14, so I want to zoom into axials 15-21 to pin down exactly where to cut the mask inferiorly.

content.text: sheet axial 4–26/137 (8 slices) | v1 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm identifying where the tumor and nerve are located on the slices, noting the tumor region starts around k=18 and up, while the thin nerve below k=17 should be erased, along with stray tail regions at low and very high k values. I'm planning to use polygon-based erasing covering the full slice extent for the ranges that need clearing.

To do this properly I need to place marks on an axial view near the tail region, so I'll check axial slice 10 with coarse marks to locate corner points around the tail area before drawing the erase polygon.

content.text: axial 10/137 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I notice at axial 10 there's a bright hazy blob in the clean image that the mask doesn't fully cover, suggesting the tumor continues inferiorly beyond what's currently marked, possibly extending down toward k=0 based on similar bright structures seen in earlier slices.

Since the volume starts at k=0, the tumor could extend below the field of view. I should check the coronal and sagittal views at this region's coordinates to trace continuity — mapping the axial pixel position to the corresponding coronal/sagittal index to see if the mass connects through those slices.

sagittal 100/181 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The coronal slice at 90 shows a lobulated bright region extending below the main mass, suggesting a second tumor lobule extending past the mask toward the volume edge. I'm also noting tubular bright structures above the mass, likely representing vessels or nerves running superiorly, and trying to distinguish which one connects directly to the mass.

The inferior lobule in the sagittal view appears hazy but contiguous with the main mass through a narrow neck, which makes me think it's a plexiform tumor extension rather than a separate structure. I want to verify this by checking axial slices around levels 8-12 with crop marks near the blob to confirm its connection and brightness relative to the confirmed tumor region.

content.text: axial 10/137 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 16/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at the round blob around (380,320) in the left panel, scaling it against the 10mm marker puts its diameter near 8mm — likely a nerve fascicle bundle, possibly the tibial nerve involved with tumor extension.

In the coronal 90 view, the mass bottom at y=470 is followed by a lobulated bright region at y=500-570, separated by a gap, suggesting continuing tumor beads along the nerve. Given the lesion's likely nerve sheath origin, this extension probably belongs in the annotation — I'll try adding a positive point near mark 25, which sits inside the blob, to see if the model expands the current mask.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 90.1 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 1–105, coronal 47–104, sagittal 88–137 | change +2.2 mL / -1.2 mL | tool calls 17/40, prompts 2/15 | point add (1 mark(s)) | image: axial 54, coronal 76, sagittal 113 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking:
That single point edit isn't working well enough, so I need to decide whether the inferior lobule should be part of the mask. I'm zooming into the sagittal slice near 100 to trace where the main mass ends and check that small bright round structure just inside the bottom edge of the field of view.

Tracking the blob across axial slices k=4 through k=20, it stays roughly in the same spot, just fading in and out, so painting a polygon across that slice range rather than a single point click seems like the better approach, since I'm unsure if the model propagates 3D edits automatically.

content.text: axial 14/137 | crop mask | marks edges | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 18/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
At axial slice 14, the bright region near (340,300) looks fuzzy, likely a transitional area with edema or tumor, making it ambiguous. The mask reasonably covers the lobule's bright core around slices 14-24, though it's quite small below slice 8 — I'll accept the mask from slice 6 onward.

The more important question is the superior extent around slices 90-105, where a tail extends toward the proximal nerve. In coronal slice 90, I see a bright tubular structure extending superiorly from the mass, about 8mm wide, along with a similar diagonal structure to the left — these look like vessels (possibly the popliteal vessels running alongside the nerve) rather than tumor tail, so I'll skip them. I want to clean up the upper tail region and check a small spot at the posterior margin, so I'll review axial slices 84-105 in an 8-slice sheet to confirm.

content.text: sheet axial 80–105/137 (8 slices) | v2 | tool calls 19/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: Looking at the upper tail around axial slices 90-105, I notice it tracks the posterior muscle edge, likely edema along the fascia near the gastrocnemius/soleus rather than true tumor, so I'm planning to erase the mask for slices k≥91 to remove this tail.

content.text: axial 94/137 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 20/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: I'm noticing a faint hazy bright region that could be the tumor tail edge, so I'm marking out coordinates and building a covering mask polygon around that area.

Now shifting to the lower tail of the mask at axial 1, looking at the lobulated inferior portion. I want to cross-check sagittal 100 and coronal 90 again and run seg_candidates to catch any tissue that might have been missed.

Final review of v3: volume 89.3 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 1–90, coronal 47–104, sagittal 88–137 | tool calls 25/40, prompts 2/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).

Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "6324" to save it.

content.text: case N32 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v3 | final volume 89.3 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 26/40, prompts 2/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I saved the final mask for case N32 (version v3) with medium confidence. It is a single component of 89.3 mL covering the large bright mass in the right posterior calf.

- **Main mass:** the outline follows the tumour edge in axial, coronal and sagittal views.
- **Upper end:** I erased a thin tail above axial slice 90, where the mask had run along the posterior muscle edge.
- **Lower end:** I kept a small inferior lobule down to the bottom of the volume, because it connects to the mass and looks like a nerve extension. It is hazy and could be nerve or edema rather than tumour, so this part is the least certain.
- **Candidates rejected:** the automatic candidates were mostly vessels or the grey rim around the mass, so I did not add them.

I used 26 of 40 tool calls and 2 of 15 model prompts.
